overview: Albania is a country in the Balkans, on the eastern shores of the Adriatic and Ionian seas. Its capital and largest city is Tirana. Albania was ruled by the Ottoman Empire for more than four centuries and declared independence in 1912. After decades of strict communist rule that cut it off from much of the world, it became a multi-party democracy in the early 1990s, and it joined NATO in 2009.

geography.text: Most of Albania is mountainous, with the Albanian Alps in the north and long ranges running down the country. A strip of coastal plain lies along the Adriatic, while the south faces the Ionian Sea. Albania shares three large lakes with its neighbours: Lake Shkodër with Montenegro, Lake Ohrid with North Macedonia, and Lake Prespa with North Macedonia and Greece.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters on the coast; the mountains inland are much colder, with heavy snow.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Brown bears, wolves and lynx live in the mountains, and the double-headed eagle on the flag is based on the golden eagle.

history.text: Albania's lands were part of the Roman and Byzantine empires before the Ottomans took control in the 1400s, despite fierce resistance led by the national hero Skanderbeg. Albania declared independence in 1912. After the Second World War, Enver Hoxha's communist government cut the country off from almost the whole world for four decades, until protests brought multi-party democracy in the early 1990s.

events.title: Skanderbeg dies
events.text: He had held off Ottoman armies for 25 years; more than four centuries of Ottoman rule followed.

events.title: Independence declared
events.text: Albania declares independence from the Ottoman Empire in the port of Vlorë.

events.title: Communists take power
events.text: Enver Hoxha begins four decades of hard-line, isolated rule.

events.title: First free elections
events.text: Multi-party elections follow the fall of communism.

events.title: Joins NATO
events.text: Albania becomes a member of the NATO alliance.

government.text: Albania is a parliamentary republic. Voters elect the 140-member parliament, which chooses the Prime Minister to run the government and also elects the President, whose role is mostly ceremonial. Albania is a candidate to join the European Union.

economy.text: Albania was one of the poorest countries in Europe when communism ended in 1991, and it has grown quickly since. Tourism along its Adriatic and Ionian coast now brings in a large share of its income, alongside farming, mining and hydropower, which produces almost all of its electricity. Money sent home by Albanians working abroad is also important.

culture.text: Albanian is a language of its own, not closely related to any other living language. Albanians follow a code of honour called besa, a promise that must never be broken, which led many families to shelter Jews during the Second World War. Iso-polyphony, a style of folk singing in several voice parts, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

items.title: Bunkers
items.text: Hundreds of thousands of concrete bunkers were built under communism; some are now cafés and museums.

items.title: Berat and Gjirokastër
items.text: Two Ottoman-era towns of stone houses, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Mother Teresa
items.text: The nun famous for her work in India was born to an Albanian family in Skopje.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Byrek, flaky pastry filled with cheese or spinach, and tavë kosi, baked lamb with yoghurt, are favourites. Meals often end with strong coffee.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Iso-polyphonic singing, with a drone under several voice parts, is listed by UNESCO. Albanian writer Ismail Kadare is famous worldwide.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Summer Day on 14 March welcomes spring with a special cake called ballokume. Weddings can last several days.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport in Albania, and the national team reached its first major tournament at Euro 2016. Weightlifting has brought Albania some of its best international results.

items.title: Euro 2016
items.text: Albania's first major football tournament, where it won a group game against Romania.

items.title: Euro 2024
items.text: Albania qualified again, topping its qualifying group.

didYouKnow: Albanians nod their head to mean 'no' and shake it to mean 'yes'.
Under communism, Albania banned private cars; in 1990 there were only a few thousand in the whole country.

keyPeople.name: Skanderbeg
keyPeople.text: Held off the Ottoman Empire for 25 years in the 1400s.

keyPeople.name: Mother Teresa
keyPeople.role: Nun and Nobel Peace Prize winner
keyPeople.text: Born to an Albanian family in Skopje; she worked with the poor in Kolkata.

keyPeople.name: Dua Lipa
keyPeople.text: Born in London to Albanian parents from Kosovo.
